tagline: Up the Virgin River and straight through the canyon wall.
intro: From I-15, SR 9 runs east through Hurricane and La Verkin, climbs past mesas and goes through Virgin, Rockville and Springdale into Zion National Park beside the North Fork of the Virgin River. There it turns up Pine Creek Canyon, climbs the switchbacks into a tunnel through the canyon wall, and comes out on the east side to leave the park for Mount Carmel Junction. The national byway covers La Verkin to the east entrance. The state byway mapped here takes in all of SR 9.
The upper road was built from 1927 to 1930, and the rock from its tunnel was dumped out through the side windows into the canyon.

moments.title: Grafton
moments.text: A cotton-growing settlement worn down by Virgin River floods, it is now said to be the most photographed ghost town in the West, with Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid among its films.

moments.title: Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel
moments.text: The tunnel runs 1.1 miles inside the wall of Pine Creek Canyon, keeping a steady distance from the cliff face, with galleries cut through to let in light and air.

moments.title: Checkerboard Mesa
moments.text: Just short of the east entrance a white sandstone summit towers 900 feet over the road, scored into a checkerboard by the bedding of ancient dunes and by the weather.

practical: The park entrance fee applies even to through traffic. Vehicles 7 feet 10 inches wide or 11 feet 4 inches tall or larger need a paid escort through the tunnel, and semi-trailers, bicycles and pedestrians are not allowed in it.
